analyst_view.overall: Early view: NEC (12th, 7 points) and Rennes (17th, 6) are close in the table but play very different games: NEC's European matches have averaged more than four goals, while Rennes have drawn three of four, two of them 0-0. NEC arrive in form under Dick Schreuder after beating Omonia 3-1 and winning 3-2 at Utrecht, where Dusan Tadic scored twice.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, which is high. I lean lower: Rennes have conceded only three goals in four European games with two goalless draws, and they were without top scorer Esteban Lepaul through injury in October. NEC at home should make it lively, but 3.8 assumes both sides score freely.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. NEC's equaliser against Omonia came from a Tjaronn Chery corner and they attack with energy at home, while Rennes are happy to defend in numbers, which fits a split close to the site's.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Neither side's European games have been bad-tempered, so I stay with the number until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.4 shots. I lean lower: Rennes' games in this competition have been short on chances (two 0-0 draws) and they will be happy to slow this one down. NEC will push, but around 26 looks more realistic.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target. For the same reason I lean lower: Rennes have allowed only three goals in four games and Brice Samba made key saves in the 2-2 at Juventus, so I'd expect closer to 9.
